_comment: What KIND of thing a Hub repo is - dated data, reviewed on a day, exactly like the uploader
allowlist beside it. Read by ModelKinds.WillNotServe.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. The browse request used to carry `&pipeline_tag=text-generation`, a
SERVER-side filter whose reason spec 6.4.2 gave in four words: 'drop embedding-model noise'.
That was true on 2026-08-08. Measured against the live Hub on 2026-08-23 across all eleven
allowlisted orgs it hid 1549 of 3093 repos: every current Gemma and Qwen GGUF is tagged
`image-text-to-text`, 1309 repos carry no tag at all, and unsloth's #2 repo by downloads
(Qwen3.8-27B-GGUF, 6.3 M) is one of the untagged. It could not be widened in place either -
`pipeline_tag` is SINGLE-VALUED like `author=` (two values return ZERO rows), so an N-kind
server filter is N requests per org. The question moved here.
A DENY-SET, NOT AN ALLOW-SET, AND THAT IS THE POINT. The defect above IS an allow-set of one
that stopped being true when the world moved. An allow-set of three re-arms the same trap with
a longer fuse: every tag HF invents after today would be hidden silently. So an unrecognised
tag PASSES, the same way an absent one does - an unreviewed tag is a form of 'not told', which
is R78's shape. The failure directions are not symmetric: a mistake here costs one odd row on a
shelf, and a mistake in an allow-set makes a real model invisible.
The tag is UPLOADER FREE-TEXT and the mistakes go both ways - measured the same day:
L3-Super-Nova-RP-8B (a Llama-3 roleplay finetune) is tagged `summarization`, and
Qwen3.8-Couture-Engine-27B (a qwen35 finetune) is tagged `robotics`. Both are kept.
`unservable_kinds` - what llama-server cannot serve as a chat model. Each entry was measured
on the allowlist on 2026-08-23 with the rows that carry it:
text-to-image / image-to-image / image-to-video / text-to-video / image-text-to-video /
image-text-to-image  -> 22 rows, archs flux, wan, qwen_image, lumina2, ltxv. Diffusion GGUFs;
llama.cpp's registry does not know a single one of these archs.
automatic-speech-recognition -> 7 rows, archs asr, sortformer, qwen3vl, qwen2.
text-to-speech               -> 3 rows. One of them declares its architecture as the literal
string 'this model cannot be used as LLM, use it via --model-vocoder
in TTS examples', which is as close to a signed confession as data gets.
feature-extraction / sentence-similarity / text-ranking -> 14 rows. Embedders and rerankers:
llama-server loads them, and not as something you can talk to.
DELIBERATELY KEPT, do not 'complete' this list - each is an ordinary causal LM with an odd tag:
translation (9: madlad400-3b-mt, hunyuan-dense, gemma4), summarization (1), robotics (1),
text-to-3d (1: LLaMA-Mesh, arch llama - it emits TEXT), video-text-to-text (1: SmolVLM2),
visual-question-answering (1: OpenCaption-4B-VL), audio-text-to-text (1: ultravox).
Excluding them would be a CAPABILITY judgement, and gatto's rule for those is that they are
measurements (`audition`) or maintainer rulings, never a default. The TheBloke exclusion in the
uploader allowlist is what one looks like when it has been argued.
`embedding_architectures` - review item 4, and the ONLY signal that reaches the case it is for.
An untagged `gemma-embedding` repo carries no pipeline_tag AND no `causal` key, and llama.cpp's
architecture registry KNOWS the arch, so `SupportedArchitectures.WillNotLoad` is false too.
MEASURED rows today: lmstudio-community/embeddinggemma-300m-qat-GGUF,
ggml-org/embeddinggemma-300M-GGUF, ggml-org/bert-base-uncased. The rest of the list is the
same kind from llama.cpp's own LLM_ARCH_NAMES, reviewed the same day - they have no rows on the
allowlist right now and are here because 'excluded by accident of tagging' is what this file
exists to stop.
TWO NAME TRAPS CAUGHT WRITING IT, pinned by a test so they are not 'completed' back in:
`pangu-embedded` is Huawei's REASONING LLM, not an embedder; `t5` is generative seq2seq that
llama.cpp runs (madlad400 is one). Neither belongs here.
_file_sidecar_comment: R80 (2026-08-23). A repo ships FILES beside the model that are not the model. These are dropped
before anything prices them, because HubSearch.Pick returns `bestGpu ?? bestRam`: a 0.86 GB draft
head that fits the graphics card beat every real quant of a 26B model on 6, 8 and 12 GB cards.
Measured through LookupAsync against the real tree of unsloth/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-GGUF - four of
five machine shapes offered a draft head as the model.
Each token has a measured row from the 220-tree census of 2026-08-23 (107 files matched, every
one a genuine sidecar, zero over-matches):
mtp      81  multi-token-prediction heads. e.g. mtp-Qwen3.8-27B-BF16.gguf at 5.95 GB - which is
1.76 bits/weight for a 27B model, so NO size rule catches it. The names earn their
keep on this row alone.
imatrix  13  an importance matrix is not weights at all.
dflash    9  e.g. dflash-kquant.gguf, 1.63 GB for a 30B model = 0.43 bits/weight.
eagle3    4  speculative-decoding heads.
LEADING for mtp/dflash/eagle3, ANYWHERE for imatrix - R80's shape, measured against the
alternative before being written: a first-or-last reading matches the SAME 107 files, so the two
are equivalent on today's data and the tighter one was ruled.
NEVER a bare Contains, and never the repo id. unsloth/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-MTP-GGUF is a real REPO
whose name carries MTP; measured, its FILES do not. The day a publisher puts the word in a file
name, a middle-position token must still read as a model name.
eagle3 and NOT bare eagle: EAGLE-3 is the speculative head, and NVIDIA ships real
vision-language models called Eagle. Only a token with a measured row belongs here.
THE CENSUS WAS RUN TWICE AND THE FIRST RUN WAS WRONG. A leading-token grep reported exactly
mmproj and mtp - a claim about the pattern (lesson 17's corollary). A discovery pass keyed on
SIZE instead, reporting whatever word each suspect actually carried, found dflash, eagle3 and
imatrix too. Add a kind the same way: discover, then name it.
mmproj is NOT here - it is a PROJECTOR, a different destination, and ModelDiscovery.IsProjector
has always owned that convention.
